label: rejected

evidence.V1: Front/3q/silhouette read as a bare tree, but the branches are uniform tusk/horn curves (reads as antlers) and a visible seating failure (branch end cap curling back into the trunk at the crown/fork) caps V1 at 1.
evidence.V2: Big trunk and five branches with three tiny twig spurs; no medium/small detail (broken stubs, knots, bark splits), branches are all the same tapered tusk.
evidence.V3: Stiff: straight pointed spike trunk top, identical horn-curve branches; the hooked branch end visibly bolted onto the trunk (fork/crown close-ups) caps V3 at 1.
evidence.V4: Inconsistent: smooth rounded branches vs razor-thin knife-edge root flares (roots close-up) and needle-sharp trunk/branch tips.
evidence.V5: Visible branch shells end with exposed rounded caps resting on the trunk instead of fusing (fork close-up, 202 cross-shell overlaps); faceted trunk strips next to smooth branches and a light smear patch at the root base.
evidence.V6: Single bark brown in 2-3 values with lighter tips; colourways (ash, birch) stay disciplined.
evidence.V8: One white vertex-colour material, but the wave-2 nature brief asks for fused smooth organic shells: branches are separate tubes and the trunk is hard-faceted.
evidence.V9: Static scenery: Anchored, Hull collision, CanTouch off, Color white, SmoothPlastic, origin bottom-centre.

artifacts: Branch end cap visible where a branch hooks back into the trunk (crown and fork close-ups)
Branches not fused to trunk; visible junction seams (202 cross-shell overlaps)
Razor-thin root flares with a light shading smear at the base (roots close-up)
top_fixes: Fuse branches into the trunk as one smooth shell with blended collars, and remove the branch that curls back into the trunk
Give the root flares thickness and rounded edges instead of knife-thin fins
Vary branch shapes (kinks, forks, broken stubs) so they read as wood rather than identical tusks, and blunt the spike on the trunk top
